why_fallback_not_resolution: Guard/consumer semantics differ: in FUN_10045490's loader the ten salt globals are written ONLY in the iVar18==0 branch (signature NOT found); every normal entry writes its global ONLY when the match is non-zero.

The written values (0x6b86410e,0x406b4b20,...,0x1cc648ea) are non-pointer 32-bit hash constants; none appears anywhere in GTAIV.exe (0 hits each). They are inputs to a hashed name/component lookup, not code addresses.

The signature's own literal '68 A9 54 14 51' decodes as 'push 0x511454a9', and 0x511454a9 is exactly the .data initial value of the first salt global 0x10158054. So the pattern is a build probe: it matches game code that embeds the hash constant 0x511454a9 (a 'push str; push hash; call' sequence). Its presence means the loaded build's hardcoded salts already match, so no substitution is needed; its absence triggers the substituted fallback set.
On GTAIV.exe 1.0.8.0 the probe DOES match (1 hit at VA 0xb3878c), so the ten-salt fallback branch is NOT taken at runtime on this build - it is a fallback for other builds.
